newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Transneft pipeline expects CPC stake.
newsitem.headline: Russian Transneft pipeline expects CPC stake.

text.p: The general director of Russia's oil pipeline company Transneft said he expected the monopoly to receive the government's 24 percent stake in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) project.
Valery Chernyayev told Reuters that government decrees on a transfer had been prepared and were awaiting signature.
"We expect authorisation of the transfer to take place soon," he said.

The role of Transneft, to be the operator of the project, has been a sticking point with CPC shareholders, who say a conflict of interest could arise if Russia's pipeline monopoly is also a shareholder.

CPC plans to build a $2 billion, 1,580 km (990 mile) pipeline from Kazakhstan's Tengiz oil field to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet Novorossiisk, with initial capacity of 560,000 barrels per day and a peak of 1.34 million bpd.

Chevron Corp owns 15 percent of CPC, Russia's LUKoil LKOH.RTS 12.5 percent, Mobil Corp and Russia's Rosneft 7.5 percent each, British Gas Plc and Italy's Agip SpA two percent each, and Oryx Energy Company and Kazakhstan's Munaigaz 1.75 percent each.
The remaining 50 percent is divided between Russia (24 percent), Kazakhstan (19 percent) and Oman (seven percent).
